title: Pre-Deployment Intervention: Stress Testing Anti-Scheming Training Under Distribution Shift
original_idea: Replicate simplified deliberative alignment fine-tuning on a small open-source model. Test scheming rates on in-distribution, novel role context, and novel reward framing scenarios. Measure degradation across distribution shift.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If anti-scheming training degrades under distribution shift, current safety claims are overstated. Directly informs deployment safety assurance levels. Critical finding for the field.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Replicating deliberative alignment fine-tuning, even simplified, requires understanding the technique and implementing it. Fine-tuning and designing distribution-shifted scenarios requires intermediate ML skills. Not beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning, designing three scenario categories, and measuring scheming rates across conditions. This is a full research project exceeding 30hrs for beginners.

novelty.reasoning: This idea has been directly addressed by 'Stress Testing Deliberative Alignment for Anti-Scheming Training' (arXiv:2509.15541, Apollo Research & OpenAI, September 2025). That paper replicates deliberative alignment fine-tuning on OpenAI o3 and o4-mini, tests on 26 OOD evaluations (180+ environments) covering novel role contexts, novel reward framings, and novel failure modes (sabotage, reward hacking, sandbagging), and measures degradation across distribution shift. The results show reduction from 13% to 0.4% for o3 but with imperfect generalization and remaining misbehavior cases. This is essentially the exact proposed experiment, already executed at scale with frontier models.
